title: Knowledge Check 5 - Lessons 21-25
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 21-25 - Data 360 Fundamentals. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: An agent keeps citing a procedure you retired last week, and the library reports healthy. What is the most likely cause?
options: The agent is missing the Service Planner.
The search index was not refreshed after the source changed, so it still holds the old chunk.
The running user lacks the Allow View Knowledge permission.
The org has run out of Data 360 credits.
questions.explanation: The retriever returns whatever chunk is in the index, and that chunk is stale until the stream refreshes and the index rebuilds.

questions.question: A search index for a new library never reaches ready. Where do you look first?
options: The agent's topic instructions.
The prompt template's tone settings.
The data stream, data lake and data model objects, and their mapping, which must be successful and active before the index is created.
The running user's data space name.
questions.explanation: The search index is created only after the stream, objects and mapping are all successful and active, so a stalled index is an upstream Data 360 problem.

questions.question: Which statement about re-indexing cost is correct?
options: Data libraries consume Data 360 credits, and re-indexing that re-chunks content spends more.
Re-indexing is always free and instant regardless of corpus size.
Only the LLM call consumes credits, not indexing.
Data 360 credits apply only to web search libraries.
questions.explanation: Data libraries consume Data 360 credits and each refresh that re-chunks content spends more, so re-indexing is a budgeted operation and unused indexes should be deleted.

questions.question: A consultant is chunking a well-structured help-center site and must choose the chunking configuration. Which setting does the documented website-grounding example use?
options: Fixed-size chunking with maximum overlap
Section Aware Chunking with a 1,200 token maximum and 0 overlap tokens
One chunk per entire web page with no maximum
Character chunking with title prepending disabled
questions.explanation: The documented example uses Section Aware Chunking with a 1,200 token maximum and 0 overlap tokens because the pages are well structured, whereas fixed-size, whole-page, or character chunking discard the section structure.

questions.question: Why can an oversized chunk hurt retrieval accuracy?
options: It exceeds the storage limit of the search index and is dropped
It forces the model to stop processing and return an error
It converts the chunk into structured data the model cannot read
Its embedding averages several ideas, so it matches no single question sharply
questions.explanation: A large chunk mixes many ideas into one vector, so it becomes a vague match for any one question, while the storage, error, and structured-data options describe failures chunk size does not cause.

questions.question: Which chunking choice preserves an idea that falls on the boundary between two sections?
options: Adding overlap tokens so the tail of one chunk repeats at the head of the next
Raising the maximum token count only
Removing title prepending from each chunk
Reducing the number of file extensions ingested
questions.explanation: Overlap repeats a tail of the previous chunk at the head of the following one so a boundary idea survives in at least one chunk, and the other options change size, context, or source scope without protecting the seam.

questions.question: Where does Data 360 store the vector embeddings it produces from chunked content?
options: In a Vector Data Model Object (VDMO)
In the source knowledge article's rich text field
In the prompt template's resource section
In the agent's topic instructions
questions.explanation: Data 360 converts each chunk into a vector embedding and stores it in a Vector Data Model Object, whereas the other locations hold source text, prompt configuration, or agent instructions rather than vectors.

questions.question: Which change makes a search index stale even though the source content is unchanged?
options: Adding a new retrieval filter that returns all documents
Enabling citation settings on the retriever
Changing the embedding model without rebuilding the stored vectors
Renaming the prompt template that embeds the retriever
questions.explanation: Stored vectors and a query only compare meaningfully when both use the same embedding model, so a model change without a rebuild leaves the index stale, while filters, citations, and template names do not touch the stored vectors.

questions.question: Which search type combines vector similarity with keyword matching so an exact term such as an error code is still found?
options: Vector search
Hybrid search
Chunk search
Citation search
questions.explanation: Hybrid search mixes vector and keyword signals, which is why the documented website-grounding index uses it, whereas vector search alone can miss an exact identifier and chunk or citation search are not search types.

questions.question: A consultant builds a new retriever and wants the agent to ground on the passage text and still cite its source. Which setting supplies that?
options: Setting the data source to Data Cloud
Choosing All Documents as the filter
Returning the Chunks field and enabling Citation Settings
Selecting Vector search as the Search Type
questions.explanation: Returning Chunks gives the model the passage to ground on and Citation Settings lets the agent show its source, while the data source, filter, and search type control scope and matching rather than the returned content and citations.

questions.question: Which Data 360 component does a retriever actually query to return relevant passages?
options: The search index that stores the chunked and vectorized content
The source knowledge article's live record
The agent's topic instruction set
The prompt template's instruction block
questions.explanation: A retriever searches a search index and returns relevant chunks from it, whereas the source record, topic instructions, and prompt block are not the retrieval source the retriever reads.

questions.question: Two data libraries need to retrieve different subsets of information from the same indexed content. What does Data 360 do?
options: It builds a separate search index for each library automatically
Each library has its own retriever that can point to the same search index but operates independently
It disables retrieval for the second library
It stores a copy of the vectors inside each prompt template
questions.explanation: Each Agentforce Data Library has its own unique retriever that can point to the same search index but operates independently, so separate indexes, disabled retrieval, or embedded vector copies are all wrong.

questions.question: In the runtime flow of a prompt template with a retriever, what is submitted to the LLM?
options: Only the user's original question
The prompt instructions, the user's query, and the retrieved passages fused together
Only the retrieved chunks, with no instructions
A request for the model to search the web
questions.explanation: The prompt is populated with the retrieved information and submitted with the instructions and the query fused in, so sending only the question, only the chunks, or asking the model to search are all wrong.

questions.question: Which phase produces the search index and the retriever that the runtime flow depends on?
options: The runtime phase, triggered by the user's question
The LLM generation phase
The citation phase, after the answer is written
The setup phase, completed before any user query
questions.explanation: Ingesting, chunking, vectorizing, storing, and creating the retriever all happen in setup ahead of time, while the runtime, generation, and citation phases all depend on that groundwork already being done.

questions.question: An agent returns a confident but unsupported answer even though the index holds the correct passage. Which hop should you suspect first?
options: The model, because it always ignores provided context
The embedding model, which must be rebuilt every query
The retriever, because a filter, missing field, or inactive retriever can keep the passage from reaching the prompt
The user's query, which cannot be embedded
questions.explanation: When the index is healthy but the answer is unsupported, the retriever is the most likely fault because a tight filter, omitted fields, or an inactive retriever stops the passage from reaching the prompt.
